  "draft_intents": [
    {
      "draft_id": "D0001",
      "actor": "Mexican government",
      "action": "launched a package of measures in 2022 to mitigate the effects of rising inflation on households, under the Paquete Contra La Inflación y La Carestía (PACIC)",
      "mechanism": "fuel subsidies were central; food-price measures leveraged and scaled up pre-existing social and agricultural support programs; public and private actors also took steps to limit price pass-through",
      "outcome": "the package was intended to cushion the impact of rising fuel and food prices on households",
      "dates": "2022; PACIC launched in May 2022",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF report description of government policies",
      "period_fit": "within the 2022 ruler-period",
      "limitations": "the report does not establish that all measures were effective; for some measures, impact was unclear",
      "polarity": "mixed/qualified positive",
      "methodology_ids": [
        "5B.9",
        "6B.6",
        "8B.2",
        "8B.6",
        "8B.9"
      ],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 73",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00005",
      "locator_disposition": "inspected locator page 73 exactly once"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0002",
      "actor": "Mexican government",
      "action": "used fuel subsidies to contain retail fuel prices during the 2022 global fuel-price shock following Russia's invasion of Ukraine",
      "mechanism": "subsidies reduced the domestic price of fuel, which comprised about 6 percent of the consumption basket",
      "outcome": "at their June peak, subsidies reduced fuel prices by as much as 30 percent and reduced headline inflation by about two percentage points, from a projected peak near 10 percent",
      "dates": "2022; peak effect in June 2022",
      "quantities": "up to 30 percent lower fuel prices; approximately 6 percent consumption-basket share; about 2 percentage points lower headline inflation; projected headline-inflation peak near 10 percent",
      "attribution": "IMF staff estimate",
      "period_fit": "within the 2022 ruler-period",
      "limitations": "the estimated inflation effect may be a lower bound because it excludes possible second-round effects; by early summer, falling fuel prices reduced the subsidy effect to about 0.2 percent in direct inflation contribution",
      "polarity": "positive, qualified by limitations",
      "methodology_ids": [
        "5B.9",
        "6B.6",
        "8B.6",
        "8B.7",
        "8B.9"
      ],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 75",
      "start_segment_id": "S00002",
      "end_segment_id": "S00006",
      "locator_disposition": "inspected locator page 75 exactly once"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0003",
      "actor": "Mexican government",
      "action": "administered a fuel-pricing mechanism established by presidential decree and governed by a methodology set out in 2019",
      "mechanism": "when the actual fuel price exceeded a constructed shadow price, the relevant excise rate was adjusted downward; the shadow price used a November 2018 base price updated for inflation every 15 days, a contemporaneous U.S. Gulf Coast reference price, transport costs, and a tax component",
      "outcome": "the formula was designed to track relevant fuel-cost trends while smoothing excessive upward cost pressures; subsidies were expected to decline with market prices and be substantially smaller in 2023",
      "dates": "presidential decree and methodology from 2019; operation and expected 2023 effect discussed in 2022",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF description of the statutory and methodological framework",
      "period_fit": "the implementation and expected effect fall within or immediately beyond the 2022 period; the underlying methodology predates the period",
      "limitations": "the report describes the intended mechanism and projected decline, not a complete evaluation of compliance or long-term effectiveness",
      "polarity": "qualified positive",
      "methodology_ids": [
        "5B.3",
        "5B.9",
        "8B.2",
        "8B.6",
        "8B.10"
      ],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 74",
      "start_segment_id": "S00011",
      "end_segment_id": "S00019",
      "locator_disposition": "inspected locator page 74 exactly once"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0004",
      "actor": "Mexican government",
      "action": "leveraged pre-existing supply-side and household-support policies to address food-price inflation",
      "mechanism": "programs included Sembrando Vida, Producción para el Bienestar, price guarantees, fertilizer delivery, the Liconsa milk subsidy, and subsidized food at Diconsa stores",
      "outcome": "the pre-existing programs provided instruments for a relatively rapid response to price pressures",
      "dates": "programs launched or existing before 2022; scaled or given greater attention during the 2022 rise in food prices",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF report description",
      "period_fit": "implementation and expanded use fit the 2022 ruler-period; several programs predate it",
      "limitations": "the scale was limited to around 0.3 percent of GDP; unclear policy objectives could hinder efficacy; the report does not establish broad outcome improvement",
      "polarity": "mixed/qualified positive",
      "methodology_ids": [
        "5B.1",
        "5B.6",
        "5B.9",
        "6B.2",
        "6B.3",
        "6B.6",
        "8B.2",
        "8B.6",
        "8B.9"
      ],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 75",
      "start_segment_id": "S00007",
      "end_segment_id": "S00014",
      "locator_disposition": "inspected locator page 75 exactly once"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0005",
      "actor": "Mexican government",
      "action": "scaled the fertilizer program from five to nine states and introduced an emergency fertilizer-production program as agricultural-input shortages worsened",
      "mechanism": "expanded geographic coverage and added emergency domestic production",
      "outcome": "the government increased support intended to address mounting agricultural-input shortages",
      "dates": "2022",
      "quantities": "fertilizer-program coverage expanded from 5 to 9 states",
      "attribution": "IMF report description",
      "period_fit": "within the 2022 ruler-period",
      "limitations": "the passage does not report the program's effects on farm output, prices, or beneficiary access",
      "polarity": "positive action with unestablished outcome",
      "methodology_ids": [
        "5B.6",
        "5B.9",
        "6B.2",
        "6B.3",
        "8B.2",
        "8B.6",
        "8B.9"
      ],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 75",
      "start_segment_id": "S00010",
      "end_segment_id": "S00012",
      "locator_disposition": "inspected locator page 75 exactly once"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0006",
      "actor": "Mexican government",
      "action": "announced agreements with major retailers to restrain price increases for 24 staple goods for an initial six-month period and announced tariff reductions on 21 basic goods and five food-production inputs",
      "mechanism": "retailers agreed to limit price increases without fiscal or regulatory implications for the government; import tariffs were reduced",
      "outcome": "the measures were intended to limit direct consumer price pass-through; forgone revenue from the tariff policy was expected to be small",
      "dates": "announced in May 2022; initial retailer commitment of six months; costs assessed for 2022",
      "quantities": "24 staple goods; 21 basic goods; 5 food-production inputs; approximately MEX$1.2 billion in expected 2022 forgone revenue",
      "attribution": "IMF report description and estimate",
      "period_fit": "within the 2022 ruler-period",
      "limitations": "the impact of the newer policies was unclear; free-trade-agreement exemptions and domestic production reduced the tariff policy's expected fiscal cost",
      "polarity": "mixed/uncertain",
      "methodology_ids": [
        "5B.3",
        "5B.4",
        "5B.9",
        "6B.2",
        "8B.2",
        "8B.6",
        "8B.9"
      ],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 75",
      "start_segment_id": "S00017",
      "end_segment_id": "S00020",
      "locator_disposition": "inspected locator page 75 exactly once"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0007",
      "actor": "Mexican government",
      "action": "implemented fuel and food-price support measures while rising prices placed further pressure on poor households",
      "mechanism": "fuel-price controls and scaled or pre-existing food, agricultural, milk, and subsidized-food programs were used to cushion household costs",
      "outcome": "poverty had improved modestly in rural areas by the end of 2020 but worsened in urban areas; in 2022, the measures were reported as responses to continuing pressure on poor households rather than as demonstrated resolution of that pressure",
      "dates": "2018–2022; rural and urban poverty comparison through end-2020; inflation pressures in 2021–2022",
      "quantities": "rural poverty or extreme poverty about 56.8 percent in 2020 versus 57.7 percent in 2018; urban poverty about 40.1 percent in 2020 versus 36.8 percent in 2018; minimum food-basket cost rose close to 2 percent for rural and urban households between March and June 2022",
      "attribution": "IMF report, citing CONEVAL and other sources",
      "period_fit": "partly baseline/context and partly within the 2022 ruler-period",
      "limitations": "the passage does not attribute the poverty changes specifically to the ruler; urban poverty and food-price pressures remained substantial; one cited per-capita labor-income series lacks 2020 Q2 data",
      "polarity": "mixed/negative context with qualified policy response",
      "methodology_ids": [
        "5B.8",
        "5B.9",
        "5B.10",
        "6B.2",
        "6B.3",
        "6B.6",
        "6B.10",
        "8B.7",
        "8B.10"
      ],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 73",
      "start_segment_id": "S00006",
      "end_segment_id": "S00015",
      "locator_disposition": "inspected locator page 73 exactly once"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0008",
      "actor": "Mexican government",
      "action": "operated a fuel-subsidy scheme financed in part by increased oil-export revenues",
      "mechanism": "the government subsidized higher domestic fuel costs while receiving additional revenue from higher prices for exported unrefined oil",
      "outcome": "the estimated 2022 oil-revenue windfall approximately covered the estimated domestic fuel-subsidy cost",
      "dates": "2022",
      "quantities": "estimated fuel subsidies of MEX$395.4 billion, or 1.36 percent of GDP; estimated oil-revenue gain of MEX$397.8 billion relative to the 2022 budget approved in 2021",
      "attribution": "IMF report estimate based on fuel-authority and budget information",
      "period_fit": "within the 2022 ruler-period",
      "limitations": "a further global fuel-price spike and higher refining margins could make subsidy costs exceed the oil-revenue increase, requiring substantial expenditure adjustment elsewhere",
      "polarity": "mixed/qualified positive",
      "methodology_ids": [
        "5B.1",
        "5B.3",
        "5B.6",
        "5B.9",
        "8B.3",
        "8B.6",
        "8B.9"
      ],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 74",
      "start_segment_id": "S00007",
      "end_segment_id": "S00011",
      "locator_disposition": "inspected locator page 74 exactly once"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0009",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities",
      "action": "maintained prudent macroeconomic policy conduct, strong monetary and fiscal frameworks, and no major macroeconomic imbalances",
      "mechanism": "the report identifies these conditions as placing Mexico in a relatively strong position to navigate global inflation, tighter financial conditions, weaker U.S. growth prospects, and increased risks of capital-flow reversals",
      "outcome": "Mexico was assessed as well placed to navigate the stated challenges, although difficult policy trade-offs remained",
      "dates": "2022 context",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "within the 2022 ruler-period",
      "limitations": "the assessment is broad and does not isolate the president's personal contribution or establish later outcomes",
      "polarity": "positive, qualified by remaining trade-offs",
      "methodology_ids": [
        "5B.3",
        "5B.9",
        "5B.10",
        "8B.7",
        "8B.9",
        "8B.10"
      ],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 8",
      "start_segment_id": "S00003",
      "end_segment_id": "S00004",
      "locator_disposition": "inspected locator page 8 exactly once"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0010",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities",
      "action": "supported economic recovery through improving wages and fiscal policy",
      "mechanism": "fiscal-policy support and wage improvements contributed to the pickup in domestic demand and output after late-2021 stagnation",
      "outcome": "real GDP expanded at an above-trend rate of 1.8 percent in the first half of 2022",
      "dates": "second half of 2021; first half of 2022",
      "quantities": "real GDP growth of 1.8 percent in the first half of 2022",
      "attribution": "IMF report assessment",
      "period_fit": "within the 2022 ruler-period, with late-2021 context",
      "limitations": "the report says the recovery also reflected continued catch-up momentum and does not establish that fiscal policy or wage improvements were the sole causes",
      "polarity": "positive, causally qualified",
      "methodology_ids": [
        "5B.1",
        "5B.6",
        "5B.9",
        "5B.10",
        "8B.7",
        "8B.10"
      ],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
